mainTopic: Floating impurity (טומאה צפה): its sources, the rules for carried and thrown items, and רמי בר חמא's unresolved questions
overview: The גמרא first asks for the source behind two opinions about doubtful contact with floating impurity. The תנא קמא says such a doubt is always pure, while רבי שמעון says it is impure in vessels but pure in the ground. Each view is drawn from two פסוקים that seem to clash. A ברייתא then teaches that carried or dragged impurities count as resting, so a doubt about them is impure. Thrown items count as moving, so a doubt about them is pure, except for a כזית of a corpse, something that overhangs impurity, and a זב or זבה. רמי בר חמא then asks a ladder of questions about impurity resting on something that floats. The cases are a corpse in a floating vessel, a corpse on a שרץ, a שרץ on a נבלה, and a שרץ on another שרץ. They continue with a שרץ on a melted נבלה, on שכבת זרע, and on מי חטאת floating on water. The גמרא cannot answer any of these questions, and they end in תיקו.

steps.title: What is the source for the first opinion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the תנא קמא, who says a doubt involving floating impurity is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the first תנא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the תנא קמא gets his rule that a doubt about floating impurity stays pure. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a doubt about impurity in a private place is treated as impure. The תנא קמא makes an exception when the impurity was floating, and the גמרא wants to know his source in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
The first (unnamed) opinion in the משנה
Impurity that is floating on water

phrases.english: What is the reason of the first tanna?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the תורה for the rule that a doubt about floating impurity is pure

steps.title: Two פסוקים about the שרץ explain the תנא קמא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר אבודימי points to two פסוקים: one implies a שרץ makes things impure anywhere, and the other says only on the land. Definite contact is impure, while doubtful contact with a floating שרץ is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר אבודימי said: It is written 'with any swarming thing that swarms', meaning wherever it swarms. It is also written 'upon the land'. How do these fit together? Definite contact makes one impure; doubtful contact leaves one pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק בר אבודימי answers with two פסוקים that seem to clash, and settles them so that the result matches the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק suggests a שרץ makes things impure everywhere, even in water. The other limits it to the land. The answer splits them: definite contact is impure everywhere, but a doubt counts as impure only on land. So a doubt about a floating שרץ stays pure.

keyTerms.meaning: A creeping creature whose dead body makes things impure
How so? (How do the two verses fit together?)
Definite contact with it
Doubtful contact with it

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Avudimi said:
It is written: "With any swarming thing that swarms"
meaning any place where it swarms,
and it is written: "upon the land."
How so?
Definite contact with it makes one impure,
doubtful contact with it leaves one pure.
phrases.notes: The case in mind is a doubt about a שרץ floating in water, which is not 'on the land'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אֲבוּדִימִי, כְּתִיב
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two פסוקים are reconciled: definite contact is impure anywhere, while doubtful contact is impure only on land. So a floating doubt is pure.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common method: two פסוקים that seem to contradict are both kept by applying each to a different case.

steps.title: What is רבי שמעון's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי שמעון, who splits between vessels and the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון, what is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for the source of רבי שמעון's opinion. This sets up עולא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון does not say a floating doubt is always pure. He says it is impure when the water is in vessels and pure when the water is in the ground, and this split needs its own source.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon, what is his reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of question as step 1, now asked about the second opinion
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי שמעון's split between vessels and the ground

steps.title: Spring water versus vessels: the source for רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: עולא points to one פסוק that says a spring stays pure and another phrase that says 'he shall be impure'. In vessels a floating doubt is impure; in the ground it is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: It is written 'Only a spring' (stays pure), and it is written 'shall be impure'. How do these fit? Floating in vessels: impure. In the ground: pure.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives רבי שמעון's source by settling two parts of a פסוק that seem to clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אך מעין' says water in a spring or pit stays pure. 'יטמא' says contact causes impurity. רבי שמעון applies the purity to water attached to the ground and the impurity to water in vessels. So a floating doubt is pure only in the ground.

keyTerms.meaning: A spring (water attached to the ground)
Floating
Vessels or containers
The ground

phrases.english: Ulla said:
It is written: "Only a spring" (shall be pure),
and it is written: "shall be impure" (until evening).
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.english: How so?
If it was floating in vessels, it is impure;
if in the ground, it is pure.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two parts of the פסוק are reconciled: water in the ground is pure, and water in vessels is impure.
steps.whatToRemember: Both opinions agree that floating impurity can be treated more leniently. The תנא קמא is lenient everywhere, while רבי שמעון is lenient only when the water is in the ground.

steps.title: Carried and dragged items count as resting; thrown items do not
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that doubts about carried or dragged impurities are impure, because they count as resting. Doubts about thrown items are pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: All things that are carried or dragged are impure in a case of doubt, because they count as resting. Things that are thrown are pure in a case of doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that extends the idea of 'moving' impurity. Carried and dragged things are not treated like floating ones, but thrown things are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A floating impurity has no fixed place, so its doubts are lenient. Something carried or dragged is held or touching the ground, so it counts as resting and the normal strict rule applies. Something thrown flies freely through the air, so it gets the lenient rule like a floating impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: Things that are carried
Things that are dragged
As though they are resting
Things that are thrown

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
All things that are carried or dragged —
in a case of doubt about them, it is impure,
because they count as resting.
And thrown things — in a case of doubt about them, it is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the topic of moving or floating impurity to items that are carried, dragged, or thrown
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carried or dragged impurities count as resting, so their doubts are impure. Thrown impurities are like floating ones, so their doubts are pure.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that anything in motion is lenient. Carried and dragged items move too, but they count as resting. Only thrown items get the lenient rule.

steps.title: Exceptions to the lenient rule for thrown items
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists exceptions where even a thrown item in doubt is impure: an olive-size piece of a corpse, something that covers over impurity, and anything that makes things impure above it just as below it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Except for an olive-size piece of a corpse, and something that overhangs impurity, and anything that makes things impure above it just as below it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and lists cases where the lenient rule for thrown items does not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In these cases a doubt stays impure even if the item was thrown. A piece of a corpse and something that overhangs impurity both relate to the strict laws of corpse impurity. The last clause is general, and the next step explains what it includes.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive-size piece of a corpse
Something that overhangs or covers, like a tent (אוהל)
From above just as from below

phrases.english: Except for an olive-bulk of a corpse,
and something that overhangs impurity,
phrases.notes: This is a thrown item that may have passed over impurity and formed a covering above it.

phrases.english: and anything that makes things impure
above it just as below it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lists exceptions to the lenient rule for thrown items in step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even when thrown, these impurities in a case of doubt are impure: an olive-size piece of a corpse, something that overhangs impurity, and anything that makes things impure above it just as below it.

steps.title: The last exception includes a זב and a זבה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the general clause about things that make impure above and below comes to include a זב and a זבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This comes to include a זב and a זבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the general phrase at the end of the ברייתא refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב or זבה makes impure what lies under them and also what is above them, even without touching. So a doubt involving them stays impure, even when a thrown item is involved.

keyTerms.meaning: To include
A man with a certain bodily flow that makes him impure
A woman with a similar flow outside her normal cycle

phrases.english: This comes to include a zav and a zava.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the final general clause of step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase 'anything that makes things impure above it just as below it' refers to a זב and a זבה.
steps.whatToRemember: Thrown items are lenient in a case of doubt, except for corpse impurity, something that overhangs impurity, and a זב or זבה.

steps.title: A corpse inside a floating vessel
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks about a corpse inside a vessel that floats on water. Do we judge by the floating vessel or by the corpse sitting inside it?
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked: if a corpse is in a vessel, and the vessel is floating on the water, what is the law? Do we go by the vessel, or do we go by the corpse?
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא opens a new question about floating טומאה. The corpse itself rests inside the vessel, but the vessel is floating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of טומאה צפה depends on whether the impurity is floating or resting. Here the corpse is resting, but only inside something that floats. So the question is which item counts: the vessel that floats, or the corpse that is held still inside it.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked / raised a question that has no obvious answer
Floating
We go after / we judge according to
The corpse (Aramaic)

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama asked:
A corpse in a vessel,

phrases.aramaic: וּכְלִי צָף עַל פְּנֵי הַמַּיִם, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: and the vessel is floating on the surface of the water, what is the law?
Do we go after the vessel,
or do we go after the corpse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the floating-doubt rule from earlier steps to a new, layered case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a corpse held inside a floating vessel counts as floating or as resting.

steps.title: A corpse lying on a floating שרץ
steps.stepSummary: Suppose we go by the vessel. Then what if a corpse lies on a floating שרץ? Does the weaker שרץ act like a vessel holding the corpse, or are the two together one solid impurity?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say we go by the vessel, then what about a corpse on top of a שרץ? Since this one, the שרץ, is impurity that lasts until evening, and that one, the corpse, is impurity that lasts seven days, is it like impurity placed in a vessel? Or perhaps it is one solid impurity?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds a second question on top of the first. It assumes one side of the first question, that we go by the vessel, and asks a harder case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שרץ is itself a source of טומאה, unlike a plain vessel. Since its טומאה is much weaker, one day versus seven, maybe it is like a separate container under the corpse. Or maybe, since both are impurities, they join into one solid impurity that is floating.

keyTerms.meaning: If you should say (if the first question is answered this way)
A dead creeping creature that makes things טמא
Impurity that lasts until evening (one day)
Impurity that lasts seven days
One solid, joined-together impurity

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. Each question assumes a possible answer to the one before it, like the rungs of a ladder.

phrases.aramaic: אִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר בָּתַר כְּלִי אָזְלִינַן:
phrases.english: If you say that we go after the vessel:
a corpse on top of a שרץ, what is the law?
phrases.notes: The שרץ is the one floating on the water, with the corpse sitting on it.

phrases.english: Since this one is impurity until evening,
and this one is impurity of seven days,
is it like impurity that is placed in a vessel,
or perhaps it is one solid impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר בָּתַר כְּלִי אָזְלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes the 'go by the vessel' side of step 8 and pushes to a case where the bottom item is itself impure.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a weaker impurity under a stronger one acts like a separate vessel, or joins it into one floating impurity.

steps.title: A שרץ lying on a floating נבלה
steps.stepSummary: Suppose different strengths of impurity make the bottom one count as a vessel, and the person is definitely impure. What about a שרץ on a floating נבלה? Both last only until evening, but their minimum sizes differ.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it is like impurity placed in a vessel and he is definitely impure, then what about a שרץ on top of a נבלה, with the נבלה floating? Since both are impurity until evening, is it one solid impurity? Or perhaps, since this one is an olive's size and that one a lentil's size, they are separate?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא climbs one more rung. It assumes the second question is answered 'like a vessel, definitely impure' and tests a case where the two impurities are closer to each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 the difference was length of time, one day versus seven. Here the time is the same, so that reason is gone. The new question is whether a different minimum size, כזית for נבלה and כעדשה for שרץ, is still enough to treat them as two separate items.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה
Olive-size, the minimum amount for נבלה to make things טמא
Lentil-size, the minimum amount for שרץ to make things טמא
Definitely

phrases.english: And if you say
it is like impurity placed in a vessel,
and he is definitely impure.
A שרץ on top of a נבלה,
and the נבלה is floating, what is the law?
Since both of them are impurity until evening,
it is one solid impurity.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא: הַאי כְּזַיִת וְהַאי כַּעֲדָשָׁה?
phrases.english: Or perhaps: this one is an olive's size and that one a lentil's size?
phrases.notes: He means the different sizes might make them two separate things, so the bottom one would act like a vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר כְּמַאן דְּמַחֲתָא טוּמְאָה בִּכְלִי דָּמְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes one side of step 9 and removes the time difference, leaving only a size difference.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a difference in minimum size alone is enough to separate two impurities that last the same amount of time.

steps.title: A שרץ lying on another floating שרץ
steps.stepSummary: The last rung: a שרץ on top of another שרץ. Now even the size is the same. Are they one impurity, or are they still separate because they are two bodies?
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a שרץ on top of a שרץ? Are these certainly one measure and so one impurity? Or perhaps, since they are separate from each other, not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the closest case so far in the ladder. The two items are the same kind, with the same time and the same size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every difference from the earlier steps is now removed: time in step 9, size in step 10. The only thing left is that they are two physically separate bodies. The question is whether being separate is enough to stop them from counting as one floating impurity. The next step assumes an answer and builds on it, and step 15 ends the whole ladder with תיקו.

keyTerms.meaning: One and the same minimum measure
They are separated from each other

steps.whatToRemember: The first four rungs of רמי בר חמא's ladder are: vessel versus corpse, then different time, then same time but different size, then same time and same size. Each rung removes one more difference to find what makes the bottom item count as a separate 'vessel.' The next steps go on to ask what the bottom layer is made of.

phrases.english: A שרץ on top of a שרץ, what is the law?
These are certainly one measure,
phrases.notes: So maybe they count as one impurity, and the whole thing is floating.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא כֵּיוָן דְּמִפַּסְקִי מֵהֲדָדֵי — לָא.
phrases.english: or perhaps, since they are separate from each other, not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes the 'separate' side of step 10 and removes the size difference as well.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether two identical impurities that are physically separate join into one, or stay apart so the bottom one acts like a vessel.

steps.title: A שרץ on a dissolved נבלה
steps.stepSummary: Assuming a שרץ on a שרץ counts as resting in a vessel, the גמרא asks about a שרץ on a נבלה that has dissolved. Is the dissolved נבלה a liquid, so the שרץ is floating? Or is it still food, a solid base?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that a שרץ on top of a שרץ is like something resting in a vessel, because they are two separate bodies: what about a שרץ on top of a נבלה that has melted? Since it melted, has it become a liquid? Or perhaps it is still food?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the next step up the ladder. It assumes the answer to the last question was 'two separate bodies, so the bottom one acts like a vessel.' Then it asks about a bottom layer that has melted into something like liquid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, the bottom layer was always solid. Here the question is about what the bottom layer is made of. If the melted נבלה counts as liquid, the שרץ is floating on liquid, and that is floating impurity. If it still counts as food, it is a solid base, and the שרץ is not floating.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you say': the גמרא assumes one answer so it can move on to a harder question
It is like something resting in a vessel, so it is not floating
An animal carcass that has melted or dissolved
A liquid
Food, meaning something with a solid, food-like status

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether the נבלה is still impure. It surely is. The question is only whether the melted נבלה counts as liquid, which would make the שרץ on top a floating impurity.

phrases.english: And if you say:
a שרץ on top of a שרץ,
phrases.notes: This is the question from step 11. The גמרא now assumes one answer to it.

phrases.english: since they are separate from each other,
it is like something resting in a vessel,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁרֶץ עַל גַּבֵּי נְבֵלָה שֶׁנִּימּוֹחָה, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: then a שרץ on top of a carcass that has melted, what is the law?
Since it melted, has it become a liquid,
or perhaps this is still food?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר: שֶׁרֶץ עַל גַּבֵּי שֶׁרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes an answer to step 11 (two separate bodies count as 'in a vessel') and builds the next, harder case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a melted נבלה count as liquid, so a שרץ on it is floating, or as food, so it is a solid base?

steps.title: A שרץ on שכבת זרע
steps.stepSummary: Assuming a melted נבלה still counts as food, the גמרא asks about a שרץ resting on שכבת זרע, which is a liquid to begin with.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that the melted carcass is food, what about a שרץ on top of שכבת זרע?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא assumes the melted נבלה still counts as food. Then it asks about a base that starts out as a liquid: שכבת זרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A melted נבלה could stay 'food' because it began as solid meat. שכבת זרע never was solid food, so the reason for the last answer does not obviously carry over. The question is whether a שרץ on it counts as floating.

keyTerms.meaning: Semen. It is itself a source of impurity.
'What is it?', meaning what is the law in this case

phrases.english: And if you say that it is food,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the melted נבלה from the question just before.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁרֶץ עַל גַּבֵּי שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: then a שרץ on top of semen, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes the melted נבלה counts as food (step 12) and moves to a base that was always liquid.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a שרץ resting on שכבת זרע considered floating on a liquid?

steps.title: A שרץ on מי חטאת floating on water
steps.stepSummary: Assuming שכבת זרע counts like food once it leaves the body, the גמרא asks about a שרץ on מי חטאת, which are themselves floating on ordinary water.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that once semen leaves the body it is like food, what about a שרץ on top of מי חטאת, when the מי חטאת are floating on regular water?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא assumes שכבת זרע counts like food once it comes out of the body. Then it asks the final and hardest case: מי חטאת floating on top of ordinary water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason given for שכבת זרע is that once it is separated from the body, it is treated like food. Now the question moves to מי חטאת. The case has two layers: the שרץ is on the מי חטאת, and the מי חטאת are themselves floating on ordinary water. So even if the מי חטאת might count as a solid base, it is unclear whether the שרץ on them counts as floating.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Once it is uprooted', meaning once it has left the body
Purification water: water mixed with the ashes of the red heifer
Floating

phrases.english: And if you say

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּמִיתְעַקְּרָא הָוְיָא לַהּ כִּי אוּכְלָא,
phrases.english: that since it has left the body, it becomes like food,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the שכבת זרע from the last question.

phrases.english: then a שרץ on top of purification water,

phrases.aramaic: וּמֵי חַטָּאת צָפִין עַל גַּבֵּי הַמַּיִם, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: and the purification water is floating on top of water, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר כֵּיוָן דְּמִיתְעַקְּרָא הָוְיָא לַהּ כִּי אוּכְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes שכבת זרע counts like food (step 13) and asks the last case in the ladder.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a שרץ resting on מי חטאת, which are floating on water, count as a floating impurity?

steps.title: We do not know: the questions stay open
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits it has no answer to these questions and leaves them unresolved with תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not know. Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the whole ladder of questions by saying it does not know the answers. They are left undecided.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not resolve the last question or the ones before it. In this ladder, each question assumed an answer to the one before, so all of them stay open, starting from רמי בר חמא's first question in step 8. The word תיקו marks a question that stays unanswered.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We do not know'
'Let it stand': the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: The whole ladder (corpse in a floating vessel, corpse on a שרץ, שרץ on נבלה, שרץ on שרץ, melted נבלה, שכבת זרע, מי חטאת) tests one idea: when does an impurity resting on something else count as 'floating'? None of these questions is resolved; they all end in תיקו.

phrases.english: We do not know; let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chain of questions from steps 8 to 14 without answering them.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The questions about what counts as floating impurity (טומאה צפה) remain unresolved: תיקו.
